name: Gweike G6 Split 30W
tagline: Split cabinet fiber marker with room for rotary and fixtures
tldr: Gweike G6 Split is a larger fiber marking platform with separate laser source cabinet: common format for small production. Available up to 100W; this profile covers the popular 30W tier.
mainObjective: Entry fiber marking on small metal parts

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

pros: Lowest-priced G6 Split, from $2,399 with manual lift on Gweike's US store
Three lift options: manual, electric, or electric with autofocus ($2,999)
Enough power for daily marking of tags, tools and tumblers on the standard 175 × 175 mm (6.9 in) lens
cons: Every 30W configuration was listed as sold out on Gweike's US store in October 2026
Gweike's 300 × 300 mm replacement lens is listed for the 50W and above, not the 30W
Q-switched source: no MOPA colour control (that is the separate G6 Split MOPA line)

faq.question: Is the G6 Split 30W still available?
faq.answer: On Gweike's US store in October 2026, every 30W G6 Split configuration ($2,399 to $2,999 depending on lift and colour) was listed as sold out, while the higher-power models were in stock. Check availability before planning around it. The G6 Split MOPA 30W ($4,099 and up) is a different, colour-capable machine.

faq.question: What can the 30W engrave, and how fast?
faq.answer: It uses a Raycus Q-switched source (20–100 kHz) with a line speed of up to 7,000 mm/s according to Gweike. It handles surface marking, black marks and shallow engraving on steel, brass and aluminum. In our benchmark, a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless steel takes about 4–11 minutes; deep relief needs many passes.

faq.question: Should I buy the 30W or step up a tier?
faq.answer: The 30W is the budget option for serial numbers, tags and tool marking. If you plan deeper engraving, thin-sheet cut-outs or large plates on the 300 × 300 mm lens, the next tier up (from $3,899 with manual lift) is the better fit, since Gweike only lists that lens from the 50W upward.

standoutFeatures.title: Split cabinet at the lowest G6 price
standoutFeatures.body: From $2,399 with manual lift, the 30W brings the G6 Split layout (separate source cabinet, room under the head for rotaries and fixtures) at roughly the price of a compact integrated fiber machine.

standoutFeatures.title: Sized for marking work
standoutFeatures.body: Raycus Q-switched source, 20–100 kHz and up to 7,000 mm/s line speed per Gweike. For serial numbers, logos and QR codes on metal, extra power mainly shortens deep jobs, which this tier is not meant for.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 30W SKU on Gweike G6 Split. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Fix parts firmly; start with low power test squares on scrap metal. Rotary adds complexity: budget time to learn indexing.
primaryUse: Desktop fiber marking for jewelry-scale and test jobs

editorialDepth.advantages: Gweike G6 Split 30W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom (50W, 70W or 100W) or a different machine class.
